pr_title: mgmt: mcumgr: grp: fs_mgmt: Improve upload and download performance
pr_body:
This vastly increases the performance of file transfers using the fs_mgmt group over MCUmgr by allowing the file handle to remain open between commands instead of having to open, feek, read/write then close the file handle for each invocation.

Fixes #52075

- [X] Upload code improvement
- [X] Download code improvement
- [x] Add fs_mgmt command to close open files (i.e. clean up)
- [x] Possibly add timer for automatic clean up if an upload/download is started but abandoned part way through
- [x] Code clean up
- [x] Kconfig to control new feature to truncate file to new size upon creation (early warning of insufficient flash to upload) **should be disabled by default:** allocating e.g. 2MB on a QSPI flash is very slow, apparently
- [ ] ~~Possibly add option to revert back to old method (check flash/RAM usage)~~
- [ ] ~~Possibly add array of fs_mgmt states, one for upload and one for download, to allow for con-current upload and download by different transports (as with this patch, if using fs_mgmt on 2 interfaces at the same time, the old issue of having to open, seed, read/write, close is present whilst flipping between states)~~ will leave for another PR if this is going to be implemented
- [x] Documentation update (if needed)
- [x] Release notes update
pr_comments: We should postpone it till 3.4 and collect data on how does this improve transfers and at what cost, because this is relatively huge change and adds complexity to the fs upload/download, that we also have to check impact of race conditions like file being removed while at download.

> collect data on how does this improve transfers and at what cost

Prior to change, maximum throughput is 3KBps, after change, maximum throughput is 18KBps, likely that flash endurance is much better after change too. Tested 2 transports at once and it is similar behaviour to old method when you do that, each packet closes, opens, seeks, writes/reads. If both clients are uploading to the same file, the file would become garbled - no different than the existing behaviour.

> like file being removed while at download.

Did not try that, will give it a try and report

Old code, delete whilst file is being uploaded: upload continues, first part of file is full of nulls's.
Old code, delete whilst file is being downloaded: download aborts with error 5.

New code, delete whilst file is being uploaded: upload continues, file vanishes so uploaded data goes into the ether.
New code, delete whilst file is being downloaded: download aborts with error 5.

So not much difference, in the old method the file would be corrupt without the user knowing and in the new method the file would not exist without the user knowing, either way the upload is useless. I can't see that being fixed until file-locking support is added to filesystems

And as for why to get this in pre-3.3, we need to make MCUmgr stable for the upcoming release, I don't want to have to go through another round of stable API change requests at the architecture meeting post 3.3

> And as for why to get this in pre-3.3, we need to make MCUmgr stable for the upcoming release, I don't want to have to go through another round of stable API change requests at the architecture meeting post 3.3

OK, I'll take a look.
@nordicjm Do you still plan to get this in for 3.3?
I think with required changes and reviews that are needed, will have to leave it until 3.4

issue_context.title: mgmt: mcumgr: Improve fs_mgmt file upload/download
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
At present, the fs_mgmt upload/download functions are self contained, this means that for each command, the underlying file is opened, seeked to the desired offset, and data read/written, then the file is closed. This works, but has an enormous overhead, reducing the throughput by roughly 6 times. This can be improved by keep the file handle open (optionally, via Kconfig) so that if the same file is written to/read from, it uses the existing object without needing to open or close it, this will vastly speed up file transfers.

Also the file access hook can be simplified to run once upon file being opened or closed, instead of for each read/write.

Note that this will require locking the file object to a specific transport, to prevent data leaking or access by a different transport/connection.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Leaving it as is.
comments:
NFS does the same thing. The problem is that it is hard to tell when operation will end and how long should the file handle be opened. This will add requirements for additional timeout mechanism to close the file handle when connection breaks too long.
Currently when you can resume uploading file, as long as device does not get reset, anytime you want.

review_comments:
Why not just immediately return BUSY?
I am not sure what we are gaining here. In case this starts to return busy, whether that happens after some timeout or not, a client app will have to figure out how to pace operations anyway to prevent being bounced back.

The timeout is there because if there are 2 transports, e.g. one doing an upload and the other doing a download, it is better for all if this has a small wait to see if the other transport finishes with it rather than not waiting and having the client resend the same message again
Also, user can set this to not wait by setting CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_FS_FILE_SEMAPHORE_TAKE_TIME to 0.
Shouldn't close be resheduled or canceleded here, to limit cases where close gets invoked on some previous timeout just after semaphore gets released ad line 578?
The variables cannot be checked here, if the sempahore is taken by the other transport, they are in an undefined state, so you can't even know if a file is open
